ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the isosceles $\triangle ABC$ has a base $BC=20$ and an area of $120$. Point $F$ is on side $BC$, and $BF=3FC$. $EG$ is the perpendicular bisector of the leg $AC$. If point $D$ moves on $EG$, what is the minimum perimeter of $\triangle CDF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,\\
$\because$ EG is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment AC,\\
$\therefore$ DA=DC,\\
$\therefore$ DF+DC=AD+DF,\\
$\therefore$ when A, D, F are collinear, DF+DC is minimized, and the minimum value is the length of the line segment AF.\\
$\because$ $ \frac{1}{2}\cdot BC\cdot AH=120$,\\
$\therefore$ AH=12,\\
$\because$ AB=AC, AH$\perp$BC,\\
$\therefore$ BH=CH=10,\\
$\because$ BF=3FC,\\
$\therefore$ CF=FH=5,\\
$\therefore$ $AF=\sqrt{AH^{2}+HF^{2}}=\sqrt{12^{2}+5^{2}}=13$,\\
$\therefore$ the minimum value of DF+DC is 13,\\
$\therefore$ the shortest perimeter of $\triangle CDF$=13+5=\boxed{18}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is an isosceles triangle ABC, with base BC horizontal, A above, B at the lower left, C at the lower right; F is located on the base BC and close to C; there is an oblique line EG passing through the interior of the triangle and intersecting side AC, and the problem statement gives that EG is the perpendicular bisector of AC; point D is on EG, and the line segments DF and DC are drawn. The problem text gives BC=20, the area of the triangle is 120, BF=3FC. Reasoning: Because D is on the perpendicular bisector EG of AC, any allowed position of D satisfies DA=DC. Therefore the perimeter of triangle CDF is CF+DF+DC=CF+DF+DA. Here CF is a fixed length, so only DA+DF needs to be minimized. By the triangle inequality, DA+DF≥AF; equality is attained when A, D, F are collinear and D is the intersection point of line AF and EG, therefore the minimum value of DF+DC is equal to AF. Calculate AF and CF: The base BC of isosceles triangle ABC is 20, and the area is 120, so the altitude AH from A to BC satisfies (1/2)·20·AH=120, giving AH=12. Because ABC is an isosceles triangle with BC as the base, the altitude AH also bisects the base, BH=CH=10. Also BF=3FC and BC=BF+FC=20, so 4FC=20, FC=5, BF=15. Thus the distance from F to the midpoint H of the base is HF=BF-BH=15-10=5. From right triangle AHF, AF=sqrt(AH^2+HF^2)=sqrt(12^2+5^2)=13. Therefore the minimum perimeter is CF+AF=5+13=18.
